name: Container Restaurant
description:
ABOUT THE SAMAN CONTAINER RESTAURANT

Every SAMAN container restaurant leaves our Bengaluru or Greater Noida plant as a finished dining venue: structure, insulation, lining, flooring, electrical distribution, kitchen-zone surfaces and service openings complete before the trailer is loaded. On site there is no fit-out phase. The unit is craned onto prepared ground, services are connected, and the room is ready for furniture the same day.

WHAT THE PRICE BUYS

The base specification price covers the welded MS structure, stainless-steel lining in the kitchen zone, mineral wool insulation in walls and roof, the finished floor, doors, glazed service openings, and the complete electrical package with distribution board, MCB and RCCB protection and earthing. The reference build is the 20x10x8.5 ft floor at ₹4,00,000 ex-factory, ex-GST, and the ladder runs from ₹2,20,000 at 10x10 up to ₹8,83,200 at 40x12. GST at 18 percent is shown alongside every figure on this page. Kitchen equipment, furniture, freight and site connection are quoted as separate lines so you can see exactly where each rupee sits.

HOW BUYERS DECIDE BETWEEN THE SIX FLOORS

Covers decide it. Under twenty covers, the 20 ft bodies do the work of a full outlet on a fraction of the ground rent. Above that, the 40 ft bodies add a genuine back-of-house, and the 40x12 flagship separates guest and kitchen circulation with its second door. The size explorer above carries the working detail for each floor: weight, panel count, electrical base, clearance and transport route.

SITE, POWER AND WATER

Firm, level, compacted ground or a simple plinth carries any size in the range. Power is an ordinary site connection sized to the estimated load shown on each tab, and plumbing terminates at connection points ready for your water supply and drainage. Nothing about the site work requires a structural contractor.

ORDERING

Send the enquiry with your covers target and plot dimensions and a fixed-price quotation follows within 48 hours. Delivery runs 7 to 21 working days from confirmation. Roughly half of what we build is customised, so the door schedule, window positions, counter length and finish palette can follow your drawing rather than ours.

5-year structural warranty and 1-year finishing warranty as standard; finishing warranty extendable to 2 years on request, confirmed at quotation. Service life is 20 to 25 years under proper use and maintenance, and that is a service life, not a warranty period. SAMAN POS India Private Limited is the manufacturer, not a reseller: ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 certified, NSIC and Udyam registered, with 500+ projects delivered across 15+ states.

THE DINING ECONOMICS THIS BUILDING IS DESIGNED AROUND

A restaurant lives or dies on covers per shift against rent per month, and this format attacks both sides of that ratio. On the revenue side, every square foot arrives usable on day one; there is no dead month where the room exists but cannot seat anyone. On the cost side, the asset depreciates on your books instead of vanishing into a landlord's wall, and if the location fails the test, the restaurant leaves with you. Operators who have lost a fit-out to a bad lease once tend to never build one into a rented site again, and they are a large share of who buys this product.

Plot economics push the same way. Restaurant-viable frontage in Indian cities rents at restaurant rates whether you build on it or park on it, so the months saved reaching first service are the highest-value months in the whole project. Work the arithmetic before choosing a size. A 17-cover floor turning twice an evening serves 34 dinners; three times, 51. Put your average ticket against that and the size question usually answers itself. Where the numbers say 25 covers and the plot says 20 ft, the honest answer is to take the 20x10 now and plan the 40 ft body for the second site, because an overcrowded room damages repeat trade faster than a small one does.

PLANNING THE ROOM: KITCHEN LINE, PASS AND SEATING

The 8 ft and 10 ft widths force useful discipline. In the 20 ft bodies, the kitchen occupies one end wall with the pass facing the room, and seating runs to the door; service distance stays short enough that one server covers the floor. In the 40 ft bodies, the kitchen takes the rear quarter behind a partition, the pass becomes a proper counter, and the dining run supports zoned seating: window pairs, a family cluster, and counter stools where the width allows. The 40x12 adds the second door, and with it the circulation pattern of a real restaurant, guests entering one way while service and stores move the other.

Tell us the menu style at the drawing stage. A grill-led menu positions the exhaust hood and its duct run differently from a steam-led one, a beverage-heavy format moves refrigeration forward, and a delivery-plus-dine-in hybrid needs the rider handover window placed where it does not cross the dining sightline. All of this is fabrication-stage layout work that costs nothing on the drawing and a great deal after delivery.

WHY THE HEAVIER SPECIFICATION EXISTS

Set this page's table against the standard cafe range and the differences are deliberate. The base frame steps up to 150x75x5 mm because a dining room carries live load across its whole span every evening, not just at a counter line. The floor moves to 24 mm cement board with waterproofing because a restaurant floor is washed like a kitchen floor, all of it, nightly. Roof insulation reaches 100 mm because a room where guests sit for an hour must hold its temperature without the AC shouting over conversation. And the kitchen zone carries stainless-steel lining because commercial cooking splashes oil at wall height and inspection regimes look there first. None of these rows is decoration; each answers a way restaurants punish buildings that cafes do not.

POWER, WATER AND THE EQUIPMENT SCHEDULE

Restaurant equipment loads run well past cafe loads, and the electrical package is planned against your equipment schedule rather than a generic one. Deep freezers, tandoors with blowers, dishwashers and espresso machines each get named circuits at the drawing stage, so the distribution board arrives labelled for the kitchen you are actually running. Water follows the same logic: the sink line, the dishwash point and any water-treatment stage are plumbed to marked positions, with waste falling to a single outlet you connect to your site's disposal arrangement. Where a site runs a grease trap, and most dining sites should, it sits outside the unit on the waste line, and we position the outlet to make that connection short.

GETTING A 40-FOOT RESTAURANT TO YOUR PLOT

The 20 ft bodies travel as routine freight. The 40 ft bodies are planned moves: an over-dimension check on the route, a long trailer, and a crane at the destination rather than a hydra. None of this is exotic, thousands of such moves run every week, but it rewards early planning. Send us the plot location with your enquiry and the transport assessment happens before you commit, not after. The freight ladder at the end of this page gives the band; the quotation fixes the figure. Roaming versions of the same trade are covered by the transportable food truck bodies, which carry a different structure for the road.

LICENCES AND INSPECTIONS, HONESTLY STATED

Food business registration and licensing sit with the operator, as they do for any premises, and requirements vary by state and by turnover. What the building contributes is a space that inspects well: food-safe surfaces where regulators expect them, washable flooring with no cracked grout lines, segregated electrical circuits with proper earthing, and documentation, drawings, specification and test records, that answers questions before they are asked. Operators moving from informal setups regularly report that the inspection conversation changes when it happens inside a factory-finished space.

STAFFING AND SERVICE FLOW BY SIZE

The floor you choose sets the team you need, and it is worth staffing the plan before signing the order. The 10x10 and 20x8 run on two people, a cook and a counter hand, with the counter hand covering the tables. The 20x10 and 20x12 add a dedicated server at busy hours, still inside a three-person shift. The 40 ft floors are four to six person operations at service: two in the kitchen, one at the pass, and floor staff scaled to the covers. None of this is a rule, but shifts planned against the room rarely bleed wages the way shifts planned against ambition do.

Service flow matters as much as headcount. In the smaller bodies, orders move over the pass directly and the room self-manages. In the 40 ft bodies the pass counter becomes the control point: plates queue there, riders collect there in hybrid formats, and the second door on the 40x12 lets stores and staff enter without crossing a full dining room. Operators who run delivery platforms alongside dine-in should say so at the drawing stage, because a rider window placed wrong turns every peak hour into a doorway argument. Operators running takeaway-led counters alongside dining should also read the lighter cafe formats before fixing the fleet.

OPENING TIMELINE FOR A RESTAURANT OPERATOR

A restaurant has more moving parts than a counter business, and the format's advantage is that most of them run in parallel with fabrication. While the unit is on the shop floor, the operator closes registrations, finalises the menu and supplier lines, orders equipment against the socket plan, and hires the kitchen team. Equipment installs the week the building lands, into circuits already named for each machine. Trial service runs inside the finished room days after placement, and the pattern we see repeatedly is a soft opening inside a fortnight of delivery, on a site that was bare ground a month before.

KEEPING THE ROOM INSPECTION-READY, YEAR AFTER YEAR

A dining room ages on its cleaning regime, and the material choices here assume a hard one. The kitchen zone's stainless lining wipes to bare metal; the anti-skid floor is laid to be hosed and squeegeed nightly without finding a seam to soak into; the washable ceiling and wall surfaces take degreaser without shedding finish. The steel exterior asks for a wash and an inspection glance at the coating each season, and a repaint cycle measured in years. Deep-clean days need no contractor: everything a crew can reach, a crew can clean. What deserves an annual look is the sealing at penetrations and the roof drainage path, both five-minute checks that keep small issues small.

WHEN THE FIRST RESTAURANT WORKS: THE SECOND SITE

The buyers who return for a second unit teach the useful lesson: they standardise. Same size where the market matches, same drawing with the openings mirrored where the plot demands, same equipment schedule so staff move between sites without retraining. A second identical room halves the management cost of the third, and because each building is an asset rather than a leasehold improvement, the pair together become collateral and balance-sheet weight in a way two fit-outs never do. Where the second site outgrows the first, the range's ladder means the move up is a specification conversation, not a new supplier search.

QUESTIONS RESTAURANT BUYERS ASK

Can it hold a full commercial kitchen? The provision is built for one: named equipment circuits, exhaust path, water and waste at marked points. The equipment itself is yours, chosen for your menu, and we wire for your list at the drawing stage without charge.

What about toilets for guests? A washroom position can be built into the 40 ft bodies at the drawing stage, or handled as a separate site facility where the plot already has one. State the requirement in the enquiry and the drawing reflects it.

Is the dining room air conditioned? AC provision is standard and the insulation depths are specified for conditioned dining. The number of units depends on size and glazing extent, and is stated on your electrical drawing.

How do two units work together? Some operators pair a 40 ft dining body with a second unit as dedicated kitchen or stores. That is a site-planning exercise we draw for you; the buildings themselves need no modification to stand adjacent.

Can the exterior match my brand? Yes, and it should. Cladding colour, facade material and the signage frame are drawing-stage choices, priced as customisation lines. A dining brand's building is its billboard on any road it stands beside.

Do you provide the furniture? No; tables and seating are your selection for your concept. What the drawing guarantees is that the layout you plan actually fits, with service circulation proven on paper before fabrication.

What happens at monsoon? The shell is sealed steel with tested roof drainage, and the entrance detail sheds water away from the door line. Site drainage is the one thing to plan: the base should stand proud of standing-water level, which is a plinth-height decision made before delivery.

How is the price split at quotation? Four lines, kept separate deliberately: the unit at base specification, customisation itemised choice by choice, freight to your pin code from the ladder below, and GST at 18 percent on the whole. Nothing folds into anything else, so a comparison against any other supplier is line for line rather than guesswork.

Can I inspect the build mid-fabrication? Yes, at either plant, Monday to Saturday, 9 am to 8 pm IST, and buyers of 40 ft units especially are encouraged to visit at the lining stage, when the layout is visible but still adjustable.

WHAT SEPARATES THIS FROM A CHEAP CONTAINER CONVERSION

The market also offers dining rooms cut from used shipping containers by small workshops, and a buyer comparing prices should compare builds. A converted box starts life optimised for cargo, not people: every window is a structural wound that must be re-engineered, the steel arrives with a decade of salt exposure, and insulation is an afterthought fitted into corrugations never meant to hold it. This page's product is fabricated new around its openings, its insulation cavity and its kitchen from the first weld, which is why the frame table above reads like a building specification rather than a repair log. The platform disclosure stands in the opening paragraph for exactly this reason: buyers deserve to know which of the two markets they are standing in.

A NOTE ON RESALE AND RESIDUAL VALUE

Because the building is movable, it holds a market when your plans change. A maintained unit re-sells to the next operator, redeploys to your own next venture, or converts to a different use, stores, a site office, a staff room, with interior work only. Fit-outs die with their lease; this asset gets a second act, and financing conversations go noticeably easier when the lender can repossess something that moves.

THE COMPANY STANDING BEHIND THE ROOM

SAMAN POS India Private Limited has manufactured portable buildings since 2009, incorporated 2019, from its own plants at Bengaluru and Greater Noida, delivering 500+ projects to 3,000+ happy customers across 15+ states with a 200+ member team. ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 certified, NSIC and Udyam registered, ZED Bronze and DPIIT Startup India recognised. Manufacturer, not reseller. Standard products carry a 7-day non-defective return window, new and unused; custom and site-specific builds are not eligible for non-defective return, with defects raised within 3 days and refunds within 7 days of approved inspection. The warranty stated above applies as written, and the freight ladder below completes the price picture.

FREIGHT AND DELIVERY CHARGES

Freight is quoted as its own line so the unit price stays comparable across suppliers. The ladders below are tentative bands for an open trailer from our nearer plant, North or South zone alike; the exact figure is confirmed with your quotation once the delivery location and order are confirmed, and may move slightly with the route and return-vehicle availability. ODC charges, where a size needs over-dimension clearance, depend on the state and are confirmed the same way.

Delivery is free within Bengaluru city, and free across Delhi NCR: Ghaziabad, Gurugram, Faridabad, Noida and Greater Noida.

Units up to 20 ft in length travel on a 20 ft open trailer. Longer bodies travel on a 40 ft open trailer.

mainEntity.name: How many covers can a single 40-ft container restaurant actually seat at table service?

acceptedAnswer.text: Plan for 16 covers at fine-dining table spacing or up to 24 covers at faster-tempo restaurant spacing using a mix of 2-top and 4-top tables. Growing past 24 covers usually means adding an outdoor deck for table extension (workable in most Indian climates seven to nine months a year) or moving to a multi-container layout. The 16–24 band fits the seat-density profile of most Indian standalone full-service restaurants.

mainEntity.name: Can the kitchen and the dining area really share one 40-ft container without FSSAI airflow issues?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — the FSSAI airflow direction (clean-to-contaminated zone separation) is built into the fitout. The kitchen zone is sealed at the service pass by a finished partition wall; cooking exhaust draws upward and out through the hood, not laterally into the dining area; the kitchen-side and dining-side ventilation are designed as separate paths from the start. The principle is the same one used by every standalone Indian restaurant with an open kitchen visible to diners. What changes here is just that the partition runs the width of a 40-ft container instead of the width of a brick room — physics is identical, FSSAI compliance is identical.

mainEntity.name: Can I add an outdoor seating deck around the container to grow my cover count beyond 24?

acceptedAnswer.text: Outdoor decks are how most container restaurant operators in India scale covers past the in-unit ceiling. Budget 200–400 sq ft of outdoor space alongside the container — a wooden deck, paved area, or a tensile shade structure depending on your site climate — and you can add 20–40 outdoor covers to the 16–24 inside, giving operating capacity of 40–60 total at peak. Outdoor covers add to your FSSAI footprint declaration and may need a separate municipal NOC for outdoor service depending on local rules. The container is the building; the deck is your expansion option.

mainEntity.name: Ready to Plan Your Container Restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Share four things and we come back within 24–48 hours with a layout drawing, an itemised quote, and a delivery and crane schedule: your starting site location, your target cover count (or your menu and table mix if you'd prefer us to back into the count for you), brand-finish preferences (wood interior, exterior colour, signage zone), and your target opening date. Standard fabrication runs 21–35 working days at our Bangalore (Gopasandra) or Greater Noida (Jalpura) facility — the closer-located factory ships to you to minimise transit. Crane unloading and on-site installation are included in the build price within India.
